articles.title: IIT Graduate Turned 'Guru' Arrested in Mathura Over Exploitation Allegations
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 29-year-old IIT graduate has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura for allegedly posing as a spiritual guru, sexually exploiting young women, and using photographs and videos of the acts to blackmail them and their families.

body.html:
A 29-year-old IIT graduate has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura for allegedly posing as a spiritual guru, sexually exploiting young women, and using photographs and videos of the acts to blackmail them and their families.

The accused, identified as Abhishek Mishra from Odisha, operated under the religious alias "Adikarta Narayan Das." He holds a degree in Mechanical Engineering from IIT Roorkee, where he studied between 2017 and 2021. Police arrested him following a complaint filed by a young woman from Chhattisgarh and have registered a rape case against him.

According to police, Mishra had been living in the Radhakunj area of Mathura for nearly four years, presenting himself as a Kathavachak (religious storyteller). To expand his influence, he ran a YouTube channel named "Radha Kripa Amrita," where he delivered sermons in both Hindi and English. He also maintained a professional profile on LinkedIn under his assumed name.

Investigators allege that he used these platforms to identify and target young women, particularly those with engineering backgrounds. Police claim he would establish contact through his online content and gradually manipulate women into distancing themselves from their families and moving in with him.

At one point, around 24 young men and women were reportedly living together at his residence in Mathura. Police allege that once women came under his influence, he would propose a Gandharva Vivah — a traditional form of Hindu marriage based on mutual consent — and use it as a pretext for exploitation.

Investigators further claim that he administered milk laced with intoxicants under the guise of offering 'Prasad' before sexually assaulting women and recording the acts. Obscene photographs and videos recovered from his mobile phone have been seized as part of the investigation.

Police also allege that Mishra extorted money from the families of those staying with him and repeatedly attempted to lure other young women from the surrounding area. Around six months before his arrest, the family of one woman reportedly arrived to take her home, following which Mishra and his associates allegedly created a disturbance.

According to police sources, Mishra's mother, who had initially stayed with him, later left due to his conduct. While he initially lived in rented accommodation, he subsequently built his own house in the area.

Police said that many of those residing with him eventually left after becoming suspicious of his activities. Investigators allege that he initially brainwashed followers to ensure their loyalty.

The investigation is ongoing to determine how many women may have been targeted and exploited by the accused.

articles.title: Speeding Car Mows Down 65-Year-Old Woman in Vadodara
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 65-year-old woman lost her life after a speeding car allegedly rammed into her from behind on Ajwa Road in Gujarat's Vadodara district. The fatal incident was captured on CCTV, and footage of the crash has since gone viral on social media, drawing widespread attention and concern.

body.html:
A 65-year-old woman lost her life after a speeding car allegedly rammed into her from behind on Ajwa Road in Gujarat's Vadodara district.

The fatal incident was captured on CCTV, and footage of the crash has since gone viral on social media, drawing widespread attention and concern.

According to preliminary reports, the woman was walking along the road when the speeding vehicle struck her from behind. The impact proved fatal, and she died as a result of the injuries sustained in the crash.

Videos circulating online reportedly show several occupants stepping out of the vehicle after the accident. Reports suggest that the car was carrying foreign nationals at the time of the incident.

The exact circumstances that led to the crash remain under investigation. Police are examining CCTV footage and gathering other evidence to determine how the accident occurred and whether any negligence or other offences were involved.

A case has been registered, and authorities have launched a detailed probe into the incident.

Police officials said further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation. Additional details regarding the identities of those involved and the sequence of events are expected to emerge as the inquiry progresses.

The viral CCTV footage has sparked outrage on social media, with many users demanding strict action against those responsible for the woman's death.

articles.title: Speeding Dumper Triggers Chaos: Bus Crashes Into Hotel Shed After Massive Impact in Mehsana
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major road accident was reported at Daran Chowkdi in Kadi town of Gujarat's Mehsana district after a speeding dumper truck rammed into a stationary private company bus from behind.

body.html:
A major road accident was reported at Daran Chowkdi in Kadi town of Gujarat's Mehsana district after a speeding dumper truck rammed into a stationary private company bus from behind.

The impact of the collision was so severe that the bus reportedly went out of control and crashed into the shed of a nearby hotel. The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed in the area.

According to reports, the dumper driver sustained serious injuries and was immediately shifted to a hospital for treatment. No other casualties have been confirmed so far.

Authorities have launched an investigation to ascertain the exact cause of the accident. Further details are awaited.

articles.title: Former Sarpanch’s Only Son Killed in Thar-Scorpio Crash, BKU Leader Booked
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Fresh details have emerged in the fatal Thar-Scorpio collision that took place late Saturday night near Asgarpur village on the Kala Amb Road in Haryana's Yamunanagar district.

body.html:
Fresh details have emerged in the fatal Thar-Scorpio collision that took place late Saturday night near Asgarpur village on the Kala Amb Road in Haryana's Yamunanagar district. The accident claimed the life of 25-year-old Hrithik, the only son of a former village sarpanch, while several others, including occupants of the Thar, sustained serious injuries.

According to police, the head-on collision occurred around midnight and involved a Mahindra Thar and a Scorpio travelling in opposite directions. The impact was so severe that the Scorpio reportedly overturned multiple times before coming to a halt. Dashcam footage and videos recorded shortly before the crash have since gone viral on social media.

Investigators have identified the Thar driver as Rao Farukh, a resident of Nakur in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district and the city president of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Tikait). Police have registered a case against him and launched an investigation into the incident.

Police said Rao Farukh was travelling with his nephews, Moin Rao and Sameer Rao, when the accident occurred. All three sustained serious injuries and were taken to Uttar Pradesh for treatment, which initially delayed confirmation of their identities and medical condition.

Speaking about the incident, Rao Farukh said he had travelled to Moginand village near Kala Amb to congratulate his brother-in-law, who had recently been elected village head. While returning around 12 am, he claimed that the bright headlights of an oncoming Scorpio impaired his vision, resulting in the collision.

According to Farukh, the crash caused his head to strike the Thar's windshield, leaving him bleeding, while his nephews suffered injuries to their heads, eyes, ears, noses and necks. Relatives travelling behind them reportedly rushed the injured to Kala Amb Hospital before they were shifted to Saharanpur for further treatment.

The deceased, Hrithik, was a resident of Lahadpur village and the only son of former village head Rajendra. He was travelling in the Scorpio along with his cousin Lalit Saini and friends Rajat and Harsh when the accident occurred. Hrithik later succumbed to his injuries during treatment, while the other occupants suffered serious injuries.

An emotional dimension to the tragedy has also emerged. According to Harsh's father, Subhash, Harsh had returned to India after being deported from the United States in November 2025. During his stay in America, he had become close friends with Hrithik. On Saturday, Harsh and his younger brother Rajat had travelled to meet Hrithik, and the group was returning when the fatal accident took place.

Police are examining multiple aspects of the crash, including vehicle speed, road conditions and visibility. Viral videos recorded before the accident have also sparked debate online, with many social media users raising concerns about alleged overspeeding, distraction while driving and the use of high-beam headlights on poorly lit roads.

Investigating officer Kamal Kumar of Sadhaura Police Station said the Thar's registration was traced to Dehradun and that the driver has been contacted. He confirmed that a case has been registered and that further legal action will be taken as the investigation progresses.

Authorities said a detailed probe is underway to determine the exact sequence of events and establish responsibility for the fatal collision.

articles.title: Kerala Horror: Toddler Found With 51 Injuries, Mother and Partner Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A horrifying case of alleged child abuse and murder has shocked Kerala after a one-and-a-half-year-old boy was found with dozens of injuries across his body. Police have now arrested both the child's mother and her partner in connection with the case.

body.html:
A horrifying case of alleged child abuse and murder has shocked Kerala after a one-and-a-half-year-old boy was found with dozens of injuries across his body. Police have now arrested both the child's mother and her partner in connection with the case.

The victim, Arshid, died on May 29 after being admitted to hospital. The case came to light when Ashkar, 31, the partner of the child's mother, took the toddler to a private hospital in Panavoor, claiming he had choked while eating lunch. The child was later shifted to SAT Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

A post-mortem examination reportedly revealed around 51 injuries of varying ages and severity on the toddler's body, along with severe internal bleeding in the head and other parts of the body. Investigators said the findings pointed to prolonged and repeated physical abuse. Police also reported burn marks suspected to have been caused by cigarette stubs.

Following the medical findings, Nedumangad Police arrested Ashkar on murder charges.

In a significant development, the child's mother, Akhila, 21, has also been arrested. Police have booked her on charges of abetment to murder and cruelty towards a child.

According to investigators, Akhila was aware that her son had allegedly been subjected to continuous torture for more than a month but failed to intervene, seek help or inform authorities. Police said she remained a silent spectator despite repeated incidents of abuse.

Investigators allege that Arshid was repeatedly beaten while living with Akhila and Ashkar in a rented house at Karikuzhi. The probe further revealed that the toddler had earlier suffered fractures to both arms, which were allegedly explained away as accidental injuries.

The child's maternal grandmother claimed she had repeatedly noticed injuries on the boy's body and had even lodged a complaint after becoming suspicious. Family members alleged that the child had no such injuries before he was taken to live with his mother and Ashkar.

The case gained wider attention after an old video filmed by a YouTuber resurfaced on social media. In the clip, Arshid was seen with both hands in plaster casts. At the time, Akhila reportedly claimed the injuries were caused by a bicycle fall. Investigators are now examining whether those injuries were also linked to the alleged abuse.

Public outrage intensified after details of the post-mortem findings emerged. When police brought Ashkar to the rented house for evidence collection, angry residents gathered outside and attempted to attack him. Police had to intervene and escort the accused from the area amid protests.

Neighbours told investigators that the family had been living in the locality for nearly six months and largely kept to themselves. Several residents claimed they frequently heard the child crying from inside the house.

Meanwhile, fresh allegations have surfaced from the family of Ashkar's first wife. Relatives alleged that she had also suffered severe physical abuse during their relationship and is currently undergoing treatment for injuries sustained in the past. They further claimed that Ashkar remains legally married to her and that no formal divorce has been completed.

The investigation, being supervised by the Nedumangad DySP, is continuing. Police are examining allegations of prolonged abuse, neglect and possible lapses in earlier intervention despite warning signs.

The case has sparked widespread outrage across Kerala, with citizens and child rights activists demanding the strictest possible action against all those responsible for the toddler's death.

articles.title: Bengaluru Public Prosecutor Caught Red-Handed Taking ₹5,000 Bribe, Arrested by Lokayukta
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A public prosecutor attached to the City Civil and Sessions Court in Bengaluru was arrested by the Karnataka Lokayukta Police after allegedly being caught red-handed accepting a bribe of ₹5,000 from a complainant.

body.html:
A public prosecutor attached to the City Civil and Sessions Court in Bengaluru was arrested by the Karnataka Lokayukta Police after allegedly being caught red-handed accepting a bribe of ₹5,000 from a complainant.

The accused has been identified as Savitha Naveen Patil, 55, who was serving as a Public Prosecutor at CCH-54, Bengaluru.

According to officials, the prosecutor allegedly demanded ₹5,000 from a complainant to submit objections in a case registered at the Chennamanakere Achukattu Police Station.

The complainant, Manjunath, 40, a resident of Banashankari, approached the Lokayukta and alleged that the prosecutor had sought a bribe to carry out the official work.

Based on the complaint, the Karnataka Lokayukta Police registered a case under the Prevention of Corruption Act and initiated a trap operation.

During the operation conducted on June 1, the accused was allegedly caught while accepting the ₹5,000 bribe amount. Lokayukta officials immediately secured her and placed her under arrest.

The arrested prosecutor was taken into custody for further investigation. Officials said the circumstances surrounding the alleged demand and acceptance of the bribe are being examined as part of the ongoing probe.

The case has once again highlighted the continuing efforts of the Karnataka Lokayukta Police to crack down on corruption within public offices and government institutions.

Further legal proceedings are underway.

articles.title: Bengaluru Man Stages Road Protest Over Convoy Blockade While Travelling With Pregnant Wife
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: High drama unfolded on Bengaluru's Old Airport Road on Monday morning when a frustrated commuter sat down in the middle of the road to protest after traffic was halted for the movement of Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot's convoy.

body.html:
High drama unfolded on Bengaluru's Old Airport Road on Monday morning when a frustrated commuter sat down in the middle of the road to protest after traffic was halted for the movement of Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot's convoy.

According to reports, the man was travelling with his pregnant wife when traffic was stopped as part of security arrangements for the Governor's movement. Upset over the prolonged delay, he stepped out of his vehicle and staged a peaceful protest on the road, attracting the attention of traffic police personnel deployed at the spot.

Videos of the incident, which have since gone viral on social media, show the man sitting on the road while a traffic officer repeatedly requests him to move and warns him that action could be taken if he continues blocking traffic.

During the exchange, the commuter questioned the necessity of stopping traffic before the Governor's convoy had even arrived.

"I have work too. My wife is pregnant, and you've stopped us at the signal. Have you blocked the road because of the Governor? The Governor hasn't even come out of the airport yet, but you've stopped us here," he is heard saying in the viral video.

The man also voiced frustration shared by many commuters affected by VIP traffic restrictions, asking, "Is only the Governor a VIP? Are we nobody?"

The traffic officer attempted to calm the situation, assuring the man that he was important and repeatedly urging him to clear the road so that normal movement could resume.

Despite the officer's efforts, the commuter continued his protest for several minutes, demanding that traffic be allowed to move. The situation was eventually defused after the officer called for a police patrol vehicle. The man then ended his protest, returned to his vehicle and cleared the roadway.

No reports of arrests or legal action have emerged in connection with the incident.

The episode has reignited debate over traffic restrictions imposed for VIP movements in major cities, with many commuters questioning the inconvenience caused to the public, particularly during peak hours and emergency situations.

The viral video has sparked widespread discussion on social media, with users divided between concerns over security protocols and the inconvenience faced by ordinary citizens.

articles.title: Speeding Car Launches 11-Year-Old Into Air in Gwalior, Child Critical; Driver Flees After Crash
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking hit-and-run incident was reported from Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior district, where an 11-year-old boy was critically injured after being struck by a speeding car. The impact reportedly threw the child nearly 10 feet into the air before he crashed onto the road.

body.html:
A shocking hit-and-run incident was reported from Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior district, where an 11-year-old boy was critically injured after being struck by a speeding car. The impact reportedly threw the child nearly 10 feet into the air before he crashed onto the road. The entire incident was captured on CCTV.

The injured child has been identified as Pratham Sharma (11), son of Vijay Sharma. A Class 5 student, Pratham was on his way to play with his cousin, Gauransh, when the accident occurred.

According to eyewitnesses, the incident took place between 5:15 pm and 5:30 pm on Saturday(30 May 2026) in the BSF Colony area of DD Nagar under the Maharajpura police station limits. A car bearing registration number MP07 AE 7664 allegedly arrived at high speed and hit the child.

The force of the collision threw Pratham several feet into the air before he landed on the road. He suffered a serious head injury and fractures to fingers on both his hands and feet.

The child was immediately rushed to Kanha Hospital on Bhind Road, where he is undergoing treatment. Family members said his condition remains critical.

CCTV footage of the incident has surfaced, showing the moment the speeding vehicle struck the child. The footage also allegedly shows four to five young men stepping out of the car after the crash. However, instead of helping the injured boy, they reportedly left him lying on the road and fled the scene.

Pratham is a native of Sumerpur village. His father, Vijay Sharma, is a farmer. Due to family circumstances, Pratham has been living with his mother, Jhalak Sharma, at the residence of his maternal uncle, Ravish Pandey, in Gwalior for nearly a decade, where he is pursuing his studies.

The child's uncle, Ravish Pandey, alleged that representatives of the accused have been pressuring the family to reach a compromise after the accident. He claimed that the driver and his companions have remained absconding since the incident.

Following a complaint, Maharajpura police launched an investigation. Based on CCTV footage and other evidence, police have seized the vehicle involved in the crash.

Police officials said the driver and his associates have been identified and efforts are underway to arrest them. Authorities have assured that strict legal action will be taken against those responsible.

The incident has sparked outrage locally, with family members demanding justice for the critically injured child.

articles.title: Wife Jailed for Life After Acid Attack Leaves Husband Blind; Sambhal Court Imposes ₹1.75 Lakh Fine
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A court in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal district has sentenced a woman to life imprisonment for throwing acid on her husband's face and eyes, leaving him permanently blind. The court also imposed a fine of ₹1.75 lakh on the convict.

body.html:
A court in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal district has sentenced a woman to life imprisonment for throwing acid on her husband's face and eyes, leaving him permanently blind. The court also imposed a fine of ₹1.75 lakh on the convict.

Additional District Judge Gopal delivered the verdict on Monday, holding Kahkashan guilty in the case. The judgment came after more than a year of legal proceedings and 10 court hearings.

According to the prosecution, the incident occurred on March 7, 2025, in the Sadar Kotwali area. Muzaffar Ali allegedly discovered his wife, Kahkashan, with her alleged lover at their home earlier that day. Following an argument, Muzaffar went to sleep at night.

Prosecutors told the court that while he was asleep, Kahkashan allegedly threw acid on his face and eyes. The attack caused severe burns to his face, shoulder and stomach, and resulted in the loss of vision in both eyes.

Muzaffar was admitted to Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi, where he underwent treatment for nearly six months. Despite prolonged medical care, doctors were unable to restore his eyesight.

Special Public Prosecutor Narendra Kumar Yadav informed the court that a day before the acid attack, Kahkashan had allegedly attempted to poison her husband by mixing poison in his food. He further alleged that some relatives had supported her in that act, although no separate FIR was registered in connection with the allegation.

Following the verdict, Kahkashan broke down in court. Police took her into custody immediately after sentencing and sent her to jail. During the proceedings, she reportedly kept her face covered with a dupatta.

Muzaffar Ali also attended the hearing along with his mother. Due to injuries sustained in the acid attack, he covered his face with a towel during the court proceedings.

According to case records, Kahkashan, 30, a resident of Bijnor district, married Muzaffar Ali, 35, in a love marriage in 2019. The couple has two children — a five-year-old daughter and a two-and-a-half-year-old son.

The prosecution alleged that Muzaffar had repeatedly objected to his wife's alleged relationship with another man living near their residence, leading to tensions within the family.

Kahkashan's counsel, advocate Pinky Sharma, said the defence was dissatisfied with the verdict and would challenge it before a higher court. The defence questioned the delay in the registration of the case and claimed that Kahkashan had been unfairly targeted because of her love marriage. The lawyer also alleged that the defence was not given sufficient opportunity to present its arguments.

Court records show that Kahkashan's bail application was rejected by the sessions court in June 2025. She was later granted bail by the Allahabad High Court. However, after convicting her, the trial court cancelled her bail and ordered her immediate imprisonment.

The case has drawn significant attention due to the severity of the attack, which left the victim permanently blind.
